photo_prep.subject: A grey tabby cat curled up asleep on a folded mustard-yellow knit blanket, on a wooden sill beside a window, against a pale blue-grey wall. The source is already a painterly AI-made image.
photo_prep.why: No bars, borders, captions, watermark or surrounding scene: the whole image is the scene to paint.

technique.why: Paint-along, back to front, is the beginner method and the only technique with version 2 keys: wall and window first, then the wooden sill, the blanket, the cat's body, its stripes and white fur, and the face details last.

considered.name: Block in, then build up (acrylic-block-in-beginner.yaml)
considered.why_not: It has no version 2 keys (v2_step_range, v2_rules), so pipeline v3 can't plan with it; the owner also made paint-along the beginner default.

learned: The finish prompt's limited palette (ultramarine named) pushed a muted grey-blue wall to saturated cobalt on the first try; naming the wall's muted mix in the redo fixed it.

Helpers: the steps 0-1 helper was given the photo and steps 0 and 1 (setup, canvas fit, reference, finish); the plan writer was given v3/plan-brief.md with the photo, the reference and the finish, and picked its library files (picks.json, library/); the chain checker was given v3/chain-check.md and the folder chain/looks; the lesson's writer was given words/lesson (brief.md, then feedback.md twice, arc-brief.md and arc-feedback.md); the finisher (me) was given review.json's inputs, step E and steps/8-finish.md 8a to 8c's seal.

Two paints were fitted far from their plan colors (Leaf green to a blue-gray, Light gray to a mid-dark gray); the second shows as step 18's picture laying dark touches while its words ask for pale flicks. A plan naming the flicks' lightness more strongly might steer the chain; it would need a new chain, so it was left.
Several stroke cards (x-stroke, build-from-pieces, horizontal-strokes, curved-strokes, thick-to-thin, flicking) have no load or mistakes lines, so many steps have no load or watch-out line.

Detail inside big shapes: no; the tabby stripes are one repeated dark stroke over the grey, and the whiskers are a few liner lines. notes.read: A soft, simple scene: a gray tabby kitten asleep on a chunky yellow knit blanket on a wooden ledge by a sunny window. What matters is the sleeping face and the round, furry curl of the body; what's hard is drawing the curled cat and keeping the knit and fur loose. The lesson is about building the room back to front and then the kitten from simple shapes.
notes.order: Back to front: sky, wall and garden first, then the window frame and the ledge so the room is done; then the blanket, dark loops before light; then the kitten as a flat shape, shaded, given white patches, ears and nose, stripes and fur, with the sleeping face and whiskers last, where the eye lands.

steps.blend-garden-sky: The farthest thing, the sky through the window, goes on first while the canvas is bare.
steps.blend-wall: The wall is the other far thing; it runs under everything that sits in front of it.
steps.dab-dark-leaves: The trees outside go over the dry sky, dark first so the light taps can sit on top.
steps.dab-light-leaves: Sunlit tops on the leaf clumps, once the dark taps are down.
steps.block-in-frame: The frame sits in front of the garden and the wall, so it goes on after both.
steps.shade-frame: Shadowed faces make the flat frame solid; they need the white under them dry.
steps.lay-in-ledge: The ledge fills the bottom band, under where the blanket will lie.
steps.darken-ledge: Shadow on the ledge away from the window, before the light patches.
steps.light-ledge: Sunlit patches last on the ledge, dry-brushed over the dry brown; the room is then done.
steps.block-in-blanket: The blanket sits on the finished ledge, as one flat shape first.
steps.shade-blanket: Dark knit loops and the grooves give the blanket its form.
steps.light-blanket: Light loops on the tops of the rolls, over the dark ones.
steps.block-in-kitten: The kitten lies on the finished blanket, so it goes on as one flat gray shape now.
steps.shade-kitten: Dark gray turns the flat shape round before any markings go on.
steps.white-patches: The white muzzle, paws and chest go on the shaded body before the stripes.
steps.pink-ears-nose: Small color accents on the head before the stripes cross it.
steps.tabby-stripes: The stripes follow the body's curve, now that the form and white patches are set.
steps.flick-fur: Fur flicks soften the coat over the stripes.
steps.eyes-mouth: The sleeping face is the focal point and goes on near the end, on dry paint.
steps.whiskers: Thin white whiskers are the very last marks, over everything around the face.

beginner_check.summary: Five steps build a shape or place lines by structure and got a diagram: the window frame, the blanket, the kitten, its stripes and its face. The rest are blends, dabs, fills and repeated marks that the picture and words carry. Step 18's picture shows small dark touches where the words ask for pale flicks; that is left and on the page under Known problems.

block-in-frame.noticed: A frame of several pieces appears whole in one step, and where the post, crossbar and sill join isn't obvious from the picture.
block-in-frame.pieces: The tall post first, then a crossbar near the top, then a wide sill slanting down to the left, in the order the words give.
block-in-frame.checked: Against the 384-px step picture: the post sits right of the sky strip, the crossbar high on the glass and the sill slants toward the left edge.

block-in-blanket.noticed: The folded blanket appears whole in one flat shape; a beginner would not know it is an oval top over a rolled front.
block-in-blanket.pieces: A long low oval for the top, a rounded band in front of it, then both ends rounded, as the words say.
block-in-blanket.checked: Against the step picture: the blanket runs from near the window to the right edge, with a flatter top and a thicker front roll.

block-in-kitten.noticed: A whole curled animal appears in one step; it is the hardest drawing in the lesson.
block-in-kitten.pieces: A big body oval, a head circle overlapping its left end, two triangle ears, then the tail and front legs as one curved piece along the front, as the words build it.
block-in-kitten.checked: Against the step picture and the finish: the body fills most of the blanket, the head sits at the left end, one ear near the left edge and one higher up.

tabby-stripes.noticed: The stripes' placement depends on the body's curve, which a beginner would paint as straight bars.
tabby-stripes.pieces: The block-in shapes as done, then short forehead stripes, long curves over the back, and bands across the tail.
tabby-stripes.checked: Against the step picture: short marks on the forehead, long curving stripes over the back and side, bands around the tail.

eyes-mouth.noticed: A face's features: where the closed eyes and mouth sit on a tilted head isn't clear from a 384-px picture.
eyes-mouth.pieces: The head, muzzle and nose as done, then the lower eye, the upper eye toward the top ear, and the small mouth above the paws.
eyes-mouth.checked: Against the step picture: the eyes are dipping curves on a slant, the mouth just under the nose above the paws.

stages.name: Blend the sky through the window
stages.paints: The pale sky through the window
steps: Start at the top left corner of the canvas, in the narrow strip along the left edge that will be the window.
Brush side to side across the strip with Pale blue, working down. Without rinsing, pick up White and keep going lower, then stroke back up over the join while it's wet.
Pale blue sits at the top of the strip and fades to White lower down, because the sky looks lighter near the horizon.
Keep everything outside the strip as bare canvas. The wall and window frame come later.
The strip is a smooth sky that slants down toward the left edge at its bottom. Blue at the top, nearly White below, no hard line between.

stages.name: Blend the blue wall
steps: Start at the top edge of the canvas, right where the window's sky ends, and work toward the right edge.
You used Pale blue for the sky. Here it is the wall's lightest blue near the window, laid with crossing X strokes and a bigger brush instead of side to side.
Cross short strokes over each other like overlapping X shapes. Go back over the wet paint with longer side-to-side strokes where you want it smoother.
Use Pale blue near the sky strip and Wall blue farther toward the right edge, so the wall looks lit by the window. Carry it under the sky strip too, down to the ledge line.
Leave the sky strip alone, and keep the bottom band of the canvas bare. Paint straight through where the frame, blanket and kitten will go.
The wall covers everything from the window's sky to the right edge, down to the ledge line. You can still see soft criss-cross marks.

stages.name: Dab the dark leaves outside
steps: Let the sky strip dry first, or the leaves will smear into it.
Start near the top of the sky strip and tap a few loose clumps, then move down the strip.
Tap with the tips of the bristles, wiping most of the Leaf green off first. Tap one spot more where you want a clump more solid.
Most of it goes in the bottom half of the strip, where the trees are fuller. Keep the clumps loose and soft-edged, since the trees are far away.
Let the sky show between the clumps. Keep off the wall.
The strip shows soft, broken clumps of leaves from top to bottom, fuller lower down, with sky peeking between them.

Leave the darker leaves showing underneath each sunlit top, and leave the gaps of sky open.

stages.name: Block in the white window frame
steps: Let the leaves and the wall dry first, or the frame will pick up their color.
Start with the tall post that closes the window, just where the leaves and sky end and the wall begins.
Build it from simple rectangles: pull the post down in straight strokes, then lay a crossbar across the glass near the top, then a wide sill under the glass.
Keep the edges straight, and let the sill slant down toward the left edge.
Leave the sky and leaves showing in the window panes, between the frame's pieces.
A flat White frame stands around the window: posts, a crossbar and a slanting sill, with no shadows yet.

Thin the paint with water and hold the brush upright. Pull each eye as one gentle curve that dips at the middle, starting thick and lightening.
Add the second eye higher on the face, toward the top ear, then a small dark line for the mouth where the chin meets the paws.
Leave the muzzle, nose and paws clean. Only the eyes and mouth are lined.
Two calm curved lines show the closed eyes, and a small dark mouth sits under the nose. The kitten looks asleep.

stages.name: Pull the white whiskers
steps: Let the eye and mouth lines from step 19 dry first.
Start each whisker on the muzzle, close to the pink nose.
Same liner and the same thin, steady pull as the eyes. Now the paint is White, and each line is longer and tapers out over the gray.
Thin the White with water, hold the brush upright and pull each whisker out in one stroke, lightening as you go so it tapers.
Fan three or four out toward the window over the cheek and the blanket, and three or four the other way over the gray toward the chest patch.
Leave the eyes, nose and mouth clear. Keep the whiskers few and thin.
Thin, tapering whiskers fan out from both sides of the muzzle. The painting is finished.

opening.welcome: You're about to paint a gray tabby kitten fast asleep on a chunky yellow knit blanket, on a wooden ledge by a sunny window. The heart of it is the sleeping face: closed eyes, a pink nose, a soft muzzle and paws tucked in. Warm window light and cool blue shadow give it a calm, cozy mood.
opening.light: Daylight comes in through the window and falls on the kitten's head and back, the rolls of the blanket and long slanting patches of the ledge. Everything turned away from the window drops into shadow, which is why so many steps paint the lit parts and the shaded parts separately.

skills.how: You make a big shape from simple pieces: a rectangle, an oval or a circle first, then curved pieces added around it. It builds the window frame, the rolled blanket and the curled kitten. Keep the pieces simple and let them meet; only soften the joins where the shape should look smooth.

Touch down with the tip of a round brush, press so it spreads, then pull and lift so the mark ends in a point. Rows of these teardrops make the blanket's knit loops, and smaller ones fill the kitten's ears. Too much paint or a slow lift gives a blob, so use less paint and lift quickly.

Every stroke bends with the shape, running down and around it, and that's what makes the kitten look round. You use it for the dark shading and again for the muzzle, chest and paws. Keep the darker paint on the shadow side and follow the curve every time.

opening.road: First you paint the sky through the window and the blue wall, the things farthest away. Then the window gets its leaves, its frame and the frame's shadows. Next comes the wooden ledge, laid in, darkened and lit with patches of sunlight, so the whole room is finished before anything sits in it. The blanket goes on next, flat first, then dark and light knit loops. Last comes the kitten: a flat shape, then shading, its pale patches, pink ears, stripes and fur. The sleeping face is saved for the very end, because that's where the eye lands.

the-garden-view.for: Cover the far background, the sky through the window and the blue wall, with soft blended color.
the-garden-view.end: A strip of soft sky meets a criss-cross blue wall, and the band where the ledge will go is still bare canvas.

the-wall-and-window.for: Turn the sky strip into a window, with leaves outside and a solid frame around them.
the-wall-and-window.end: A window with dappled green leaves stands in a bright frame with blue shadowed faces, next to the blue wall.

the-ledge.for: Lay the wooden ledge and give it shadow and sunlight, so the room is finished.
the-ledge.end: A warm red-brown ledge runs across the canvas, with long slanting bands of sunlight near the window.

the-blanket.for: Build the folded knit blanket and give it the texture of chunky loops.
the-blanket.end: A golden knit blanket in two rolls lies across the ledge, its loops darker in the grooves and bright where the light lands.

the-kitten-shape.for: Build the kitten as one shape, make it look round, and add its pale patches.
the-kitten-shape.end: A rounded gray kitten lies curled on the blanket, with a pale muzzle, a pale chest patch and two pale paws.

the-markings-and-fur.for: Give the kitten its pink ears and nose, its tabby stripes and its soft fur.
the-markings-and-fur.end: The kitten has pink ears, a pink nose and dark tapering stripes around its head, back and tail, with soft fur on its lit back.

the-sleeping-face.for: Finish the focal point: the closed eyes, the mouth and the whiskers.
the-sleeping-face.end: The finished painting: a sleeping tabby kitten with closed eyes and fine whiskers, curled on its knit blanket by the window.

technique_picks.technique_why: A cozy scene of big simple shapes (wall, window, ledge, blanket, cat) that paints naturally back to front, with the cat built from an oval and a circle and finished with stripes and flicked fur, all within a beginner's reach.
